title: Responsable de la sécurité des Systèmes d'Information RSSI H/F
description:
Rattachement : Direction générale
Périmètre : Groupe EDL – France & international
Localisation : Siège EDL– déplacements ponctuels à prévoir
Statut : Cadre / CDI

1. Mission

Dans un contexte de forte croissance, d’internationalisation et de développement par croissance externe, EDL renforce sa gouvernance de la cybersécurité et recherche son/sa Responsable de la Sécurité des Systèmes d’Information (RSSI).

Rattaché(e) à la Direction, le/la RSSI définit et pilote la stratégie de cybersécurité du Groupe, en cohérence avec les enjeux business, réglementaires et technologiques d'EDL.

Il/elle est garant(e) de la confidentialité, de l’intégrité et de la disponibilité des systèmes et des données, notamment dans un environnement particulièrement sensible lié aux données et aux solutions de santé.

Le/la RSSI joue un rôle transversal, à l’interface entre la Direction, les équipes IT, R&D, Produit, RH, Juridique et les différentes entités du Groupe.

2. Responsabilités principales

Définir et piloter la stratégie cybersécurité

  • Définir la stratégie, la politique et la feuille de route cybersécurité du Groupe.
  • Identifier et prioriser les principaux risques cyber en fonction des enjeux métiers.
  • Définir les politiques, standards et règles de sécurité applicables à l’ensemble des entités.
  • Construire et suivre les indicateurs de performance et de maturité cybersécurité.
  • Présenter régulièrement les risques, incidents et plans d’actions à la Direction et aux instances de gouvernance.

Gouvernance, risques et conformité

  • Piloter le Système de Management de la Sécurité de l’Information (SMSI) et contribuer à la certification et au maintien des certifications ISO 27001, ISO 9001.
  • Organiser les analyses de risques et piloter les plans de traitement associés.
  • Assurer une veille réglementaire et normative : NIS2, RGPD, exigences liées au secteur de la santé, ISO 27001, etc.
  • Définir et maintenir les politiques et procédures de sécurité.
  • Piloter les audits internes et externes et assurer le suivi des plans de remédiation.
  • Participer à l’évaluation de la sécurité des fournisseurs et partenaires critiques.

Sécurité opérationnelle

En collaboration avec les équipes IT et techniques :

  • Superviser la mise en œuvre des mesures de sécurité : IAM, MFA, EDR, sauvegardes, chiffrement, segmentation réseau, gestion des vulnérabilités, etc.
  • Définir les exigences de sécurité pour les infrastructures, applications et environnements cloud.
  • Piloter la gestion des vulnérabilités et le suivi de leur remédiation.
  • Définir et tester les dispositifs de Business Continuity / Disaster Recovery.
  • Superviser la gestion des incidents de sécurité et coordonner la réponse aux incidents majeurs.
  • Organiser régulièrement des exercices de crise cyber.

Sécurité des produits et du développement

Compte tenu de l’activité d’EDL, le/la RSSI travaille étroitement avec les équipes Produit et R&D afin d’intégrer la sécurité dès la conception :

  • Définir les exigences de sécurité applicables aux produits et projets.
  • Promouvoir une approche Security by Design / Privacy by Design.
  • Participer à la sécurisation du cycle de développement logiciel.
  • Superviser ou coordonner les tests d’intrusion, audits de sécurité et revues d’architecture.
  • Accompagner les équipes dans la gestion des vulnérabilités produits.
  • Contribuer à la gestion des exigences de sécurité clients et aux réponses aux questionnaires de sécurité.

Sensibilisation et culture cybersécurité

Le/la RSSI est également responsable du développement d’une véritable culture sécurité au sein du Groupe :

  • Définir et déployer le programme annuel de sensibilisation à la cybersécurité.
  • Organiser les formations et campagnes de phishing/sensibilisation.
  • Adapter les actions aux différents publics : collaborateurs, managers, équipes techniques et dirigeants.
  • Développer les réflexes de sécurité dans les pratiques quotidiennes.

Acquisitions et transformation du Groupe

Dans le cadre des opérations de croissance externe et d’intégration de nouvelles entités :

  • Réaliser les cyber due diligences des sociétés acquises.
  • Évaluer les risques, écarts de conformité et niveaux de maturité des entités intégrées.
  • Définir les plans de sécurisation et d’intégration.
  • Harmoniser progressivement les politiques, outils et standards de sécurité du Groupe.
  • Accompagner les projets de transformation IT et les migrations de systèmes.

3. Profil recherché

De formation supérieure en informatique, cybersécurité, systèmes d’information ou équivalent, vous disposez de 8 à 12 ans d’expérience, dont une expérience significative en responsabilité cybersécurité.

Vous avez idéalement évolué dans un environnement :

  • international et multisites ;
  • en forte croissance ou transformation ;
  • soumis à des exigences fortes de sécurité et de conformité ;
  • idéalement dans les secteurs de la santé, du logiciel, du SaaS ou dans un environnement réglementé.

Vous maîtrisez notamment :

  • les référentiels ISO 27001 / ISO 9001 ;
  • l’analyse et la gestion des risques cyber ;
  • la gouvernance SSI ;
  • la gestion des incidents et de la continuité d’activité ;
  • les architectures cloud et les enjeux de sécurité associés ;
  • les principes IAM, MFA, EDR, sauvegarde, chiffrement et gestion des vulnérabilités ;
  • la sécurité applicative et les principes DevSecOps ;
  • les enjeux RGPD et, idéalement, NIS2.

Une certification ISO 27001 Lead Implementer / Lead Auditor, CISSP, CISM ou équivalent serait un plus.

4. Compétences et qualités personnelles

Au-delà de l’expertise technique, nous recherchons un profil capable de transformer les enjeux cyber en décisions business.

  • Forte capacité d’analyse et de priorisation.
  • Excellente compréhension des enjeux de risque et de gouvernance.
  • Capacité à travailler avec des interlocuteurs techniques comme avec un Comité de Direction.
  • Leadership transversal et capacité d’influence.
  • Pédagogie et excellent relationnel.
  • Autonomie, pragmatisme et sens des responsabilités.
  • Capacité à évoluer dans un environnement en construction, avec un niveau important de transformation.
  • Anglais professionnel courant.

5. Ce que nous proposons

Rejoindre EDL, c’est intégrer un Groupe en forte croissance, au cœur de la transformation numérique du secteur de la santé.

Le poste offre une forte exposition Groupe et la possibilité de construire et structurer la fonction cybersécurité dans un environnement international, en accompagnant notamment :

  • la croissance rapide du Groupe ;
  • son développement international ;
  • ses opérations de croissance externe ;
  • la montée en maturité de sa gouvernance cyber ;
  • ses enjeux de certification et de conformité ;
  • la sécurisation de solutions logicielles critiques pour le secteur de la santé.

Un rôle stratégique, transversal et à fort impact, au cœur des enjeux de confiance et de croissance d’EDL.

title: Ingénieur·e Logiciel Embarqué
description:
QUI SOMMES-NOUS ?

Smart Impulse c'est l'histoire d'un projet de fin d'études qui se transforme en un projet entrepreneurial ambitieux et engagé !

title: Valve Lead Engineer
description:
About Pangea Propulsion:

We are a company dedicated to developing advanced propulsion systems for the space industry based on three key principles: high efficiency, sustainability, and reusability. We are revolutionizing the space industry with ground-breaking innovations that allow us to offer the best performance to cost propulsion systems. Our goal is to be the propulsion provider for the next generation of spacecraft, which is essential to meet demands and compete in the booming space market of the next decade.

We are a passionate, multicultural, and multidisciplinary team pushing the boundaries of what is possible in space propulsion technology.

We have already made history by successfully testing the world's first 3D-printed Methalox Aerospike engine, marking a significant milestone for the space industry.

We are looking for talented professionals to join our international teams in Barcelona and Toulouse. We want to be a key player in improving diversity in the Aerospace sector as, in Pangea, we believe that diversity (gender, age, race, sexual orientation, beliefs, disability, culture, etc.) is a key to success. Within Pangea, everyone can grow with the same opportunities. We encourage you to apply. Individually we are different, but together we are an amazing team!

We are looking for a Senior Valve Engineer (Technical Authority) based in Toulouse.

About the role

We are seeking a hands-on valve expert who will serve as Pangea’s company-wide technical authority for valves. The mission is to build the internal capability to specify, design, analyse, source, test, qualify, industrialise, and continuously improve critical valves for our propulsion systems.

The first priority will be to assess and internalise selected valves used on Nereus, starting where technically and commercially justified with HTP-compatible valves. The scope can then expand to other valve families and propulsion programmes based on risk, recurring cost, lead time, supply-chain dependence, and strategic value.

This is a senior individual-contributor role with strong technical leadership. You will work closely with Fluidics and across Systems, Design, Analysis, Materials, Manufacturing, Quality, Supply Chain, Test, and Operations, taking decisions from first principles and carrying them through to validated hardware.

Key responsibilities

· Act as Pangea’s technical reference for valves, owning design decisions, technical reviews, risk acceptance, and the valve technology roadmap across propulsion programmes.

· Define the valve internalisation strategy and prioritise candidates using performance, safety, development risk, recurring cost, lead time, supplier dependence, and manufacturing scalability.

· Lead the initial Nereus workstream for HTP-compatible solenoid valves: capture requirements and interfaces; benchmark make-versus-buy options; select concepts; and define the development and qualification plan.

· Own the full product lifecycle—from requirements, architecture, trade-offs, detailed design, analysis, materials and sealing selection through prototyping, testing, qualification, production release, and in-service improvement.

· Develop or approve valve sizing and dynamic models covering flow capacity and pressure drop, actuation force and margin, response time, leakage, thermal effects, friction, hysteresis, fatigue, wear, contamination sensitivity, and lifetime.

· Establish verification logic, acceptance criteria, instrumentation, test matrices, and qualification evidence for nominal, off-nominal, proof, endurance, environmental, and compatibility testing.

· Ensure compatibility with HTP and, as applicable, cryogenic, high-pressure, hot, reactive, or hazardous fluids through disciplined materials, cleanliness, sealing, lubrication, and contamination-control choices.

· Resolve difficult hardware problems through structured failure investigation, test-data interpretation, root-cause analysis, corrective action, and design iteration.

· Lead technical engagement with valve, actuator, coil, seal, and manufacturing suppliers; review proposals, drawings, analyses, process controls, inspection plans, qualification evidence, deviations, and non-conformances.

· Create reusable internal standards, design rules, calculation methods, test procedures, lessons learned, and product architectures, while mentoring engineers and raising valve competence across the company.

Initial Mandate

Build a credible make-versus-buy and development plan for Nereus HTP-compatible solenoid valves, close the highest-risk knowledge gaps with analysis and testing, and leave behind a repeatable internal valve-development capability.

What you need to be successful

Education

· Master’s degree in Mechanical Engineering, Aerospace Engineering, Mechatronics, Fluid Mechanics, or a closely related engineering discipline.

· Additional specialization in fluid systems, cryogenics, mechanical design, tribology, sealing technology, materials, or control systems would be advantageous.

Experience

· 8 to 10 years or more of relevant engineering experience, with substantial direct ownership of valve or closely related fluid-control hardware.

· Demonstrated hands-on delivery of hardware from requirements and concept selection through detailed design, test, qualification, and production support.

· Deep experience with solenoid, pilot-operated, pneumatic, electro-mechanical, or comparable valves for demanding applications.

· Experience with high-pressure, reactive, hazardous, cryogenic, or high-temperature fluid systems; liquid rocket propulsion or space hardware experience is strongly preferred.

· Evidence of solving real valve failure modes and working directly with manufacturing, suppliers, inspection teams, test facilities, and non-conformance processes.

Technical expertise

· Strong command of valve architecture, fluid mechanics, actuation, sealing, tribology, tolerancing, material selection, cleanliness, and design for manufacture and assembly.

· Ability to size and analyse valves using appropriate analytical and numerical methods, and to correlate models with component and system test data.

· Proven capability investigating leakage, friction, hysteresis, pressure drop, response time, actuation margin, contamination, wear, fatigue, thermal effects, and lifetime.

· Working knowledge of qualification logic, reliability, FMEA, fracture and fatigue considerations, configuration control, and technical documentation for safety-critical hardware.

· Knowledge of HTP compatibility, decomposition hazards, compatible materials and seals, cleanliness, and safe test practices is highly valuable.

Leadership

· Strong technical ownership: comfortable making and documenting difficult decisions, while actively seeking challenge and evidence.

· System-level thinking, with the ability to connect valve behaviour to engine, propulsion-system, test-bench, and vehicle performance.

· Pragmatic judgement that balances technical excellence with safety, schedule, cost, manufacturability, maintainability, and qualification effort.

· Clear communication across disciplines and with suppliers, including the ability to turn ambiguous problems into structured plans and crisp technical requirements.

· Builder’s mindset: equally willing to work at a whiteboard, review a drawing, analyse data, inspect hardware, and support a test campaign.

Additional assets

Advanced education: Postgraduate specialisation in fluid mechanics, cryogenics, sealing, tribology, mechatronics, controls, or mechanical design.

Relevant sectors: Space propulsion, aerospace, energy, hydrogen, oil and gas, chemical processing, or other high-pressure and hazardous-fluid industries.

Specialised expertise: HTP service, cryogenic valves, high-pressure solenoid valves, pilot-operated architectures, sealing technologies, actuation systems, materials compatibility, cleanliness, or lifetime qualification.

You might just be the ideal candidate for this position or other opportunities within our organization.

We welcome applications from persons with disabilities and we can provide reasonable accommodations throughout the recruitment process and in the workplace.

description:

Eine KI-gestützte Plug-and-Play-Optimierungslösung, die den Energieverbrauch massiv senkt, Betriebskosten um bis zu 35 % reduziert und sich oft in weniger als einem Jahr amortisiert. Namen wie die SBB, der Flughafen Zürich oder Mobimo vertrauen bereits auf uns.

Unsere Software wertet Gebäude aus und steuert sie auch direkt vor Ort. Wir wachsen schnell, und der Betrieb muss mitwachsen. Genau hier kommst du ins Spiel: Wir suchen dich als Infrastructure & Operations Engineer, um aus bestehenden Grundlagen einen Betrieb zu machen, der auch bei einem Vielfachen der heutigen Grösse trägt — und um ihn danach zu verantworten!

Aufgaben

Deine Aufgaben als Infrastructure & Operations Engineer

  • Betrieb und Automatisierung: Du führst unsere bestehenden Werkzeuge zu einem durchgängigen System zusammen und entwickelst es weiter.
  • Flottenbetrieb skalieren: Du machst den Betrieb bereit für eine stark wachsende Geräteflotte in Kundengebäuden — mit verlässlichen, automatisierten Rollouts.
  • Gebäudeanlagen absichern: Du verantwortest Netzwerksegmentierung, Zugriffskontrolle und sichere Fernzugänge zu unseren Geräten und den Anlagen dahinter.
  • Plattform betreiben und härten: Du betreibst unsere eigene Infrastruktur und machst sie fit für die nächsten Jahre — von Storage über Kapazitätsplanung bis zu Runbooks.
  • Zugänge und Nachweise: Du gestaltest den Lebenszyklus von Zertifikaten, Dienstkonten und Zugriffsrechten und sorgst dafür, dass Audit-Nachweise im Alltag automatisch entstehen.
  • Präsenz: Du bist dort, wo die Anlagen stehen — bei Kundenstandorten, im Rechenzentrum, im Office in Baden oder flexibel aus dem Homeoffice.

Qualifikation

Das bringst du mit

  • Betriebs-DNA: Du bringst Systeme zum Laufen und hältst sie am Laufen. Du bringst zu Ende, was du anfängst, und übernimmst Verantwortung für das, was danach im Betrieb ist.
  • Technisches Fundament: Linux im Betrieb, nicht nur in der Anwendung — Systemd, Netzwerkstack, Fehlersuche an laufenden Systemen. Dazu Netzwerk mit Substanz: Routing, NAT, Firewalling, VPN, Segmentierung.
  • Automatisierung: Infrastruktur als Code ist für dich Alltag. Git ist deine Arbeitsweise, nicht dein Ablageort.
  • Skripting: Python und Bash, um Werkzeuge zu bauen und Daten auszuwerten. Dazu SQL, um Betriebsdaten selbst abzufragen, statt auf ein Dashboard zu warten.
  • Agentic Coding: Du arbeitest selbstverständlich mit KI-Agenten wie Claude Code, Codex oder Cursor. Du weisst, wie man eine Aufgabe so zuschneidet, dass ein Agent sie zuverlässig löst, und erkennst, wann du besser nicht delegierst.
  • Urteilsvermögen: Du kannst Code lesen und beurteilen, auch in Sprachen, in denen du nicht selbst entwickelst. Bei uns entsteht viel mit Agenten — das Prüfen und Entscheiden ist die eigentliche Arbeit, besonders wenn eine Änderung die ganze Flotte erreicht.
  • Feld- oder Flottenerfahrung: Du hast mit verteilten Geräteflotten gearbeitet oder kommst aus der Anlagentechnik und weisst, was es bedeutet, wenn ein Update ein Gebäude erwischt.
  • Sprachen: Deutsch und Englisch.

Wertvoll, aber keine Voraussetzung: Erfahrung mit Virtualisierung und verteiltem Storage, Datenbanken, Gebäudeautomations-Protokollen, Kubernetes sowie IEC 62443 oder ISO 27001 aus der Praxis. Zertifikate ohne Praxis brauchen wir nicht.

Benefits

Das bieten wir dir

  • Entscheidungsspielraum statt Zuarbeit: Du baust die Infrastruktur, die du danach betreibst. Architektur und Betriebsmodell liegen bei dir, nicht bei einem Gremium.
  • Eine Strategie statt eines Blankoblatts: Die Grundlagen sind erarbeitet. Du fängst nicht bei null an — und auch nicht in einem fertigen System, in dem nichts mehr zu entscheiden ist.
  • Ein Problem, das es so selten gibt: Eine Geräteflotte, die stark wächst, und Infrastruktur, deren Fehler nicht in einem Ticket enden, sondern in einem Gebäude. Wer Gebäudetechnik und IT-Betrieb verbinden will, findet das nicht an vielen Orten.
  • Kurze Wege: Ein kleines Team, keine Zwischenebenen, kein Konzernprozess. Was am Montag entschieden wird, läuft am Mittwoch.
  • Agentic Coding als Standard: Wir arbeiten konsequent mit KI-Agenten, finanzieren die Werkzeuge dafür und entwickeln die Arbeitsweise gemeinsam weiter. Wer das schon kann, wird hier nicht ausgebremst.

Ehrlich vorab: Wir sind ein kleines Team, und diese Rolle ist neu. Vieles wirst du selbst gestalten, statt es vorzufinden — von Runbooks bis zu Bereitschaftsregeln. Wenn dich genau das reizt, passt es gut. Wer eine eingespielte Betriebsorganisation sucht, wird bei uns nicht glücklich.

Dafür arbeitest du an etwas, das messbar wirkt: Jedes Gebäude, das effizienter läuft, zählt doppelt — für unsere Kunden und für die CO2-Bilanz.

Kein klassisches Motivationsschreiben nötig. Beschreib uns im Anschreiben stattdessen in ein paar Sätzen, woran du zuletzt gearbeitet hast und was dabei schiefgegangen ist — das sagt uns mehr als jede Floskel.

title: Sales Manager
description:
Über homer

Gemeinsam bauen, nicht alleine kaufen. Hilf uns, eine neue Form des Wohnens Wirklichkeit werden zu lassen.

Wohnen ist eine der wichtigsten Entscheidungen im Leben – und trotzdem stehen viele Menschen vor einer Wahl, die sich nicht richtig anfühlt: hohe Mieten zahlen oder sich mit einem Immobilienkauf finanziell langfristig binden.

Wir bei homer glauben, dass es einen anderen Weg gibt. Wir entwickeln genossenschaftliche Wohnprojekte, die hochwertige Architektur, langfristige Sicherheit und gemeinschaftliches Wohnen miteinander verbinden. Menschen schaffen sich ein Zuhause, ohne dafür allein Eigentum erwerben zu müssen.

Dafür suchen wir Dich. Du bringst Menschen für unsere Projekte zusammen, führst sie vom ersten Interesse bis zur Reservierung und sorgst dafür, dass aus unserer Idee gelebte Realität wird.

Deine Aufgaben

Du gewinnst Interessent*innen für unsere Wohnprojekte und begleitest sie vom ersten Kontakt bis zur Reservierung.

Du führst Informationsveranstaltungen, persönliche Gespräche und Termine vor Ort durch und machst unser Wohnmodell verständlich und erlebbar.

Du entwickelst einen strukturierten Vertriebsprozess, der Interessierte zuverlässig durch ihre Entscheidungsphase begleitet.

Du behältst den Überblick über Anfragen, Conversion Rates und Vermarktungsziele und sorgst dafür, dass wir unsere Projekte erfolgreich vermarkten.

Du baust unsere Interessentenverwaltung und das Follow-up mit CRM und KI-gestützten Werkzeugen effizient auf.

Du erschließt neue Vertriebskanäle und Partnerschaften, über die wir Menschen erreichen, für die unser Wohnmodell interessant ist.

Du arbeitest eng mit unserem Genossenschaftsmanagement zusammen, das die Mitglieder ab der Reservierung weiter begleitet.

Du denkst Marketing mit:

Du erkennst, welche Botschaften und Kanäle die richtigen Menschen erreichen, und entwickelst unsere Vermarktung gemeinsam mit dem Team weiter.

Du sorgst dafür, dass unsere Projekte verständlich, überzeugend und zielgruppengerecht präsentiert werden.

Das bringst Du mit

Du hast Erfahrung im Vertrieb und Freude daran, Menschen für ein Produkt oder eine Idee zu begeistern – idealerweise auch bei erklärungsbedürftigen Angeboten.

Du gehst aktiv auf Interessent*innen zu, führst überzeugende Gespräche und bleibst konsequent dran, bis aus ersten Kontakten konkrete Entscheidungen werden.

Du denkst in Zielen und Abschlüssen, arbeitest strukturiert mit Kennzahlen und weißt, wie Du Deine Vertriebsaktivitäten wirksam priorisierst.

Du packst selbst mit an und baust Vertriebsprozesse eigenständig auf, statt darauf zu warten, dass alles bereits vorhanden ist.

Du hast ein gutes Gespür für Menschen, kannst komplexe Themen verständlich erklären und unterschiedliche Interessen zusammenbringen.

Du nutzt digitale Tools und KI selbstverständlich, um Deine Arbeit effizienter zu gestalten und neue Wege im Vertrieb auszuprobieren.

Du identifizierst Dich mit unserer Idee, Wohnen gemeinschaftlich, nachhaltig und langfristig anders zu gestalten.

Erfahrung in der Immobilienbranche ist ein Plus, aber keine Voraussetzung.

Du bist bereit, zwischen Hamburg, Berlin und unseren Projektstandorten zu reisen.

Was wir Dir bieten

Eine Aufgabe mit Sinn: Du hilfst dabei, eine Wohnform aufzubauen, die Menschen langfristig neue Möglichkeiten eröffnet.

Verantwortung, die etwas bewegt: Du siehst unmittelbar, wie Deine Arbeit dazu beiträgt, dass unsere Wohnprojekte Realität werden.

Faire Vergütung mit Erfolgsbeteiligung: Wir bieten ein Fixgehalt und einen leistungsbezogenen Bonus. Darüber hinaus entwickeln wir ein Modell, das Mitarbeitende abhängig von ihrer Rolle am gemeinsamen Unternehmenserfolg beteiligt.

Ein starkes Team: Du arbeitest mit erfahrenen Menschen aus Architektur, Projektentwicklung und Genossenschaftsmanagement zusammen.

Aufbauen statt verwalten: Du kannst Vertriebsprozesse etablieren, neue Wege ausprobieren und Deine Ergebnisse direkt sichtbar machen.

Langfristig denken: Wir bauen homer nicht für einen schnellen Exit auf, sondern entwickeln ein Unternehmen mit einer langfristigen Perspektive.

title: Content & Community Manager (m/w/d)
description:
Deine Rolle

Wir sind HeyHoney, ein wachsendes Unternehmen mit einer treuen Community und einem klaren Produkt. Diese Community ist eines unserer wertvollsten Assets – und genau hier kommst du ins Spiel.

Bei uns erwarten dich Verantwortung, Geschwindigkeit, Flexibilität und viel kreativer Gestaltungsraum – verbunden mit der Möglichkeit und Erwartung, diesen aktiv zu nutzen.

Während unser Head of Performance & Growth die Skalierung verantwortet, machst du unsere Marke jeden Tag erlebbar: Du entwickelst unsere organischen Kanäle, unseren Content und unsere Community-Formate weiter – vom ersten Konzept bis zum fertigen Reel, vom Community-Kommentar bis zum Event.

Dabei arbeitest du eng mit Creator, UGC-Creator und Freelancer zusammen und berichtest direkt an unsere Head of Performance & Growth.

Dein Verantwortungsbereich

Content & Social Media: Du betreust und entwickelst unsere organischen Kanäle – insbesondere Instagram, TikTok und Pinterest – und hast Trends, Plattform-Logiken und neue Formate immer im Blick.

Content-Produktion: Du entwickelst Content-Ideen und setzt sie hands-on um – insbesondere Short-Form-Video. Dabei kannst du sowohl neuen Content produzieren als auch vorhandenes Material kreativ weiterdenken und daraus neue, plattformgerechte Inhalte entwickeln. Für Produktionen arbeitest du bei Bedarf mit UGC-Creator und Freelancer zusammen und steuerst diese eigenständig.

Creator & UGC: Du identifizierst relevante Creator, baust Beziehungen auf und entwickelst ein nachhaltiges Netzwerk aus UGC-Creator, Freelancer und Partner, das unsere Marke langfristig voranbringt.

Community Management: Du bist eine der Stimmen von HeyHoney. Du interagierst regelmäßig mit unserer Community, aktivierst sie und entwickelst Ideen, mit denen aus Kund echte Fans werden. Dabei entwickelst du Community-Formate, die Bindung und Retention stärken.

Community Events: Du entwickelst gemeinsam mit dem Team Ideen für Community Events und begleitest deren Umsetzung – von Planung und Partner-/Location-Auswahl bis zur Durchführung und Nachbereitung.

Launch-Support: Für unsere Kollektions-Launches entwickelst du organische Content- und Community-Ideen und verzahnst sie eng mit unseren Paid-Aktivitäten.

Analytics & Reporting: Du behältst relevante KPIs wie Reichweite, Engagement und Community-Wachstum im Blick, erkennst, welche Inhalte funktionieren, und leitest daraus konkrete Learnings und neue Content-Ideen ab.

Was du mitbringst

Du fühlst dich auf Social Media zu Hause und verstehst, warum Content funktioniert – oder eben nicht. Dabei ist uns dein Gespür für Content, Community und relevante KPIs wichtiger als eine bestimmte Anzahl an Berufsjahren.

Idealerweise bringst du mindestens ein Jahr praktische Erfahrung im Bereich Social Media, Content oder Community mit – zum Beispiel aus einer Festanstellung, Werkstudentätigkeit, einem Praktikum, Freelance-Projekten oder eigenen Social-Media-Projekten.

Du bist hands-on: Du kannst Content von der Idee bis zur Umsetzung begleiten und hast ein gutes Auge für Ästhetik, Trends und die unterschiedlichen Logiken von Instagram, TikTok & Co.

Du verstehst Content Creation: Du kannst selbst drehen und schneiden und weißt gleichzeitig, wann Creator, UGC oder Freelancer die bessere Lösung sind. Du musst dabei nicht zwingend selbst vor der Kamera stehen – wichtiger ist, dass du gute Inhalte erkennst, entwickeln und umsetzen kannst.

Du kannst Community: Du verstehst, wie aus Reichweite Interaktion und aus Interaktion echte Bindung entsteht. Wenn du bereits eine Community oder eigene Social-Media-Kanäle aufgebaut hast, umso besser.

Du schreibst markensicher: Du hast ein gutes Sprachgefühl und triffst den Ton einer modernen Lifestyle-Brand.

Du denkst in Zahlen: Reichweite, Engagement Rate, Watch Time oder Community-Wachstum sind für dich nicht nur Reporting-Zahlen. Du nutzt sie, um zu verstehen, was funktioniert und was wir beim nächsten Mal besser machen können.

Du setzt um: Du wartest nicht darauf, dass dir jeder einzelne Schritt vorgegeben wird. Du bringst Ideen ein, probierst Dinge aus, lernst daraus und treibst deine Themen eigenständig voran.

Uns ist dabei nicht wichtig, dass du schon jede dieser Aufgaben perfekt beherrschst. Wenn du Social Media verstehst, Lust hast, Verantwortung zu übernehmen, schnell lernst und HeyHoney gemeinsam mit uns weiterentwickeln möchtest, wollen wir dich kennenlernen.

Was wir dir bieten

Content, Community und Events sind bei uns bewusst noch nicht auserzählt. Das bedeutet: Du kommst nicht in ein fertiges System, sondern kannst aktiv mitgestalten.

Echter Gestaltungsspielraum: Ein kleines, schnelles Team, kurze Wege und die Freiheit, Strukturen, Formate und Ideen selbst mit aufzubauen – im direkten Sparring mit unserer Head of Performance & Growth.

Flexibles Arbeitsmodell: Wir sind Remote-First und offen für unterschiedliche Modelle – Vollzeit, Teilzeit oder Werkstudent. Entscheidend sind für uns dein Beitrag, deine Fähigkeiten und der messbare Output, nicht deine Anwesenheit im Büro.

Entwicklungsmöglichkeiten: Die Rolle kann mit dir wachsen. Wenn du Verantwortung übernehmen möchtest und zeigst, dass deine Ideen funktionieren, bekommst du bei uns den Raum dafür.

Miteinander, das zur Marke passt: Wir sind ein herzliches, offenes Team und leben den HeyHoney-Spirit auch intern – mit Augenhöhe, Vertrauen und einem wertschätzenden Miteinander, das auch über die Distanz trägt.

Lust, HeyHoney mit aufzubauen?

Dann freuen wir uns auf deine Bewerbung.

Zeig uns dabei gerne mehr als deinen Lebenslauf: Welche Accounts, Reels, TikToks oder Formate findest du richtig gut? Was hast du selbst schon umgesetzt? Welche Community oder welchen Kanal hast du mitentwickelt?

Links zu eigenen Accounts, Content-Beispielen, UGC-Projekten oder Events sind sehr willkommen. Auch eigene Projekte zählen für uns – es muss nicht alles aus einer klassischen Festanstellung stammen.

Bei HeyHoney zählt, was du kannst und einbringst – unabhängig von Alter, Geschlecht und geschlechtlicher Identität, Nationalität und Herkunft, Religion und Weltanschauung, sexueller Orientierung, einer Behinderung oder deiner sozialen Herkunft. Wir bewerten Bewerbungen ausschließlich nach fachlicher Eignung und freuen uns über jede Perspektive, die unser Team vielfältiger macht.

Wir freuen uns auf deine Bewerbung!

title: Backend Software Engineer - Application Development
description:
A World-Changing Company
 
Palantir builds the world’s leading software for data-driven decisions and operations. By bringing the right data to the people who need it, our platforms empower our partners to develop lifesaving drugs, forecast supply chain disruptions, locate missing children, and more.

The Role
 
Backend Software Engineers at Palantir build software at scale to transform how organisations use data. Our Software Engineers are involved throughout the product lifecycle, from idea generation, design, prototyping, and production delivery. You will collaborate closely with technical and non-technical teammates to understand our customers' problems and build products that solve them. We encourage movement across teams to share context, skills, and experience, so you'll learn about many different technologies and aspects of each product. Engineers work autonomously and make decisions independently, within a community that will support and challenge you as you grow and develop, becoming a strong technical contributor and engineering leader.
 
Your day-to-day workflow will vary, adapting to the requirements of our users and the technical challenges that arise. One day, you may find yourself collaborating with other engineers to architect a new system that enables a novel workflow, the next you could be fine-tuning performance to enable low-latency operational outcomes.
 
Our Product Development organisation is made up of small teams of Software Engineers. Each team focuses on a specific aspect of a product and work collaboratively to build cross functional capabilities, streamline user workflows and continuously improve our software's efficiency and reliability.
 
We’re hiring engineers who are passionate about solving real-world problems and empowering both developers and end-users to work optimally. If you’re motivated to develop reliable, performant, and scalable systems, and to design robust APIs and primitives, this role offers the opportunity to make a significant impact on our products and the people who use them.
 
Frontline
 
Foundry Software Engineers may be offered the opportunity to Frontline, an exclusive program unlike any other. This unique, short-term assignment involves being embedded with customers, allowing you to work directly with users and gain firsthand insight into how our products are used and the challenges our customers face. Unlike traditional engineering roles, Frontline immerses you in complex, ambiguous problems, empowering you to deliver impactful solutions across some of the world’s most important industries and institutions.
 
Some of our most successful products were built on the factory floor, addressing real-world problems for the world's most important institutions. These products were developed by some of our most successful product engineers, who began their careers in roles aligned with Frontline responsibilities, gaining a deep understanding of both our technology and our customers.
 
Frontliners operate across a broad spectrum of responsibilities, much like a startup CTO. They work in small teams to own the end-to-end execution of high-stakes projects. This spectrum ranges from discussing architecture and building custom web apps to conducting workshops with users and strategizing with customer executives. No two days are alike, as each day is diverse and impactful. By witnessing how customers engage with Foundry and experiencing these pain points firsthand, you’ll gain unique insights that feed directly back into our development process, helping to refine and enhance our products.

Core Responsiblities
  • Architecting, developing, and maintaining high-performance, scalable backend services that underpin our our operational data and AI systems
  • Maintaining high coding standards through the development of guidelines, active participation in code reviews, and fostering a culture of continuous improvement and knowledge sharing among your team
  • Building robust APIs for use by front-end developers and interfacing external systems, and collaborating with front-end developers to integrate user-facing elements with server-side logic
  • Designing efficient data structures and algorithms to manage large-scale and high throughput data
  • Optimizing applications for speed and scalability through performance analysis
  • Actively improve user workflows by collaborating with cross-functional teams, ensuring seamless experiences across product boundaries and a cohesive user experience

    • Technologies We Use
  • Different backend languages, including Java, Rust, Python and Go
  • Distributed systems technologies such as Kafka, Cassandra, Elasticsearch and Spark
  • Docker and Kubernetes for containerisation and orchestration
  • Industry-standard build tooling, including Gradle and GitHub

    • What We Value
  • A deep understanding of server-side logic, efficient data handling, and distributed systems
  • Strong focus on creating user-oriented workflows and solutions, crossing product boundaries to deliver cohesive and solid user workflows that ensure a seamless and intuitive user experience
  • Experience building high-quality software in a fast-paced CI/CD development environment
  • Ability to work collaboratively in teams of technical and non-technical individuals and understand how technical decisions impact the people who will use what you're building
  • Skill and comfort working in a constantly evolving environment with dynamic objectives and iteration with users
  • Active UK Security clearance, or eligibility and willingness to obtain a UK Security clearance is beneficial but not necessary

    • What We Require
  • Experience in designing and developing features and improvements, as well as supporting and maintaining, live backend systems
  • In-depth understanding of data structures, system architecture, API development for microservices frameworks, distributed systems and other backend-related concepts and best practices
  • Engineering background in Computer Science, Mathematics, Software Engineering, Physics or similar field
  • Strong coding skills with demonstrated proficiency in programming languages, such as Java, C++, Python, Rust, or similar languages
  • Strong written and verbal communication skills and ability to iterate quickly with teammates, incorporating feedback and holding a high bar for quality
    • Life at Palantir
     
    We want every Palantirian to achieve their best outcomes, that’s why we celebrate individuals’ strengths, skills, and interests, from your first interview to your longterm growth, rather than rely on traditional career ladders. Paying attention to the needs of our community enables us to optimize our opportunities to grow and helps ensure many pathways to success at Palantir. Promoting health and well-being across all areas of Palantirians’ lives is just one of the ways we’re investing in our community. Learn more at Life at Palantir and note that our offerings may vary by region.
     
    In keeping consistent with Palantir’s values and culture, we believe employees are “better together” and in-person work affords the opportunity for more creative outcomes. Therefore, we encourage employees to work from our offices to foster connectivity and innovation. Many teams do offer hybrid options (WFH a day or two a week), allowing our employees to strike the right trade-off for their personal productivity. Based on business need, there are a few roles that allow for “Remote” work on an exceptional basis. If you are applying for one of these roles, you must work from the city and or country in which you are employed. If the posting is specified as Onsite, you are required to work from an office.
     
    If you want to empower the world's most important institutions, you belong here. Palantir values excellence regardless of background. We are committed to making the application and hiring process accessible to everyone and will provide a reasonable accommodation for those living with a disability. If you need an accommodation for the application or hiring process, please and let us know how we can help.

If you suspect that you've been contacted by a scammer, we recommend you cease all communication with the individual and consider reporting them to the relevant authorities, such as the US FBI Internet Crime Complaint Center (IC3).

title: Senior Product Manager, KYB - MoonPay Enterprise
description:
MoonPay Enterprise is for builders with something to prove.

This isn't a "work on cool crypto stuff" company. It's a high-standards, high-velocity, high-accountability company building the operating system for value movement. If the internet moves information, we move value: crypto, stablecoins, tokenized assets, and whatever comes next. Four offerings make that real: fund, tokenize, trade, and spend.

MoonPay Enterprise is the fund layer built for businesses. We power how stablecoins move through real financial operations: enterprises, fintechs, PSPs, wallets, and marketplaces running their treasuries, their cross-border flows, and their stablecoin operations on us. The goal is to make moving real money at scale as predictable as any other piece of financial infrastructure, with the compliance and controls CFOs need to say yes.

AI is the default operating mode here. It's woven into every role, and we expect you to use it daily. It handles the manual work so you can deliver on what actually matters.

You'll thrive here if outcomes excite you more than process, if impact motivates you more than titles, and if you want hard problems, real ownership, and teammates who love winning, building, and doing it together.

The bar is high. The pace is real. We're building the rails that businesses run real money on, for humans and agents. MoonPay ranked #2 in Crypto Services on Fortune's inaugural Crypto 100, made Forbes' America's Best Startup Employers 2026 (Top 25 in Finance), and landed on The Sunday Times Best Places to Work two years running.


About MoonPay Enterprise

MoonPay Enterprise is one of the more operationally complex products in the stablecoin space: multiple banking providers, multiple payment rails, a growing partner base across two product lines (Orchestration and Issuance), and an active compliance surface across each. MoonPay Enterprise runs B2B, B2B2B, and B2B2C models. Partners integrate our API. Their customers become direct customers of MoonPay Enterprise for compliance purposes.

KYB is the front door. Every partner is a business. Every business customer of every partner clears KYB before a single transaction moves. Today the flow is part automated registry verification, part manual review, with different rules for the US and the rest of the world, and turnaround measured in days. That does not scale to where MoonPay Enterprise is going. KYB has to become a product: measurable, fast, API-first, defensible in front of regulators and banking partners. This is a principal seat. You set the multi-year direction for how businesses enter MoonPay Enterprise, and you own the outcome.

What You'll Own

KYB product strategy & roadmap

  • Business onboarding end-to-end, across every model MoonPay Enterprise runs: partners onboarding onto MoonPay Enterprise, businesses onboarding directly, and business customers onboarding through partners.

  • Platform altitude. KYB decisions ripple into KYC, Travel Rule capture, banking-provider onboarding, and Issuance partner diligence. Connect the surfaces; don't optimise one in isolation.

  • MoonPay Enterprise runs three KYC delivery models (reliance, outsourcing, hosted). KYB coverage is uneven across them. You decide where it expands and in what order.

  • Genuine product depth on MoonPay Enterprise is non-negotiable. Within weeks you talk fluently about KYB outcomes, UBO requirements, virtual account structures, and API behaviour. From being hands-on, not from documentation.

Onboarding funnel & conversion

  • The KYB funnel is yours: pass rate, time-to-verified against a 48-72h target, manual review rate, drop-off per step.

  • Instrument what isn't instrumented. Make approval speed and rejection quality measurable. Then move both.

  • Fix rejection UX. Today a declined business often gets a status without a reason, and the partner escalates to support to find out what is missing. Rejection reasons, retry semantics, and resubmission flows become API surface partners build on.

KYB API & partner experience

  • The KYB API surface: statuses, webhooks, document submission, and the edge cases that make business onboarding hard (sole proprietors, corporate shareholders, one person who is UBO, Director, and Representative at once).

  • Partners integrate KYB in weeks and self-serve their onboarding questions. Every "what is missing for this customer" escalation is a product gap. Close it.

Compliance as product

  • Turn compliance-approved onboarding matrices into product logic. US and non-US differ: control prong versus directors, when ownership documents are required, self-certification options. Partners should never need to read a matrix.

  • EDD triggers, high-risk classification, prohibited industries, Travel Rule capture: you decide how they show up in the product.

  • Compliance is your sparring partner, not a ticket queue. You shape how policy becomes product. They own the policy.

Vendor & provider orchestration

  • The verification stack (SumSub today) and the build-versus-buy calls around it.

  • Cost per verification, automation rate, vendor performance. Know when a second provider, a waterfall, or in-house tooling earns its place.

  • Push automation. Decide where AI-assisted review with a human in the loop replaces manual queues, and prove it does not raise risk.

  • Every new banking provider brings its own onboarding requirements. Keep KYB compatible with every rail without collecting everything from everyone.

Who You Are

  • A principal-level PM with real KYB or KYC depth. You have owned onboarding, identity, verification, or risk as a platform, not a feature.

  • High agency. You do not wait for a mandate, a brief, or perfect data. You find the problem, claim it, and fix it.

  • Full autonomy, zero to one. Hand you an unowned surface and you take it from first principles to shipped. No handover document, no waiting for direction.

  • AI-fluent by default. AI tools are your daily instruments for analysis, prototyping, and drafting. You run your own queries; analysis is not something you request from another team.

  • Compliance is a design constraint, not a blocker. You read a requirements matrix and see API design, funnel steps, and copy.

  • You know your funnel cold: pass rate, time-to-verified, manual review rate, cost per verification.

  • At home in API-first B2B. Your users are partner engineers and the businesses behind them, not consumers.

  • You have run verification vendors (SumSub, Persona, or equivalents) and know when to switch, stack, or build.

  • A multiplier for the product team around you. You raise the bar for how compliance-heavy product work gets scoped, specced, and shipped.

  • Bias to action. Reactive stewardship of an existing flow is not what we are hiring for.

title: Senior Project Manager (EMEA or USA)
description:
Company Overview:

At Panopto, we are the most customer-centric learning technology company in the world. As the leader in visual and audio-based learning, we empower organizations to share knowledge effortlessly in a capture and post-capture world. We don’t just build software; we obsess over our users’ goals to deliver solutions that truly matter. Our mission is simple: to attract the brightest talent, people like you, to Elevate the Craft and do the most impactful work of your career.

 

Panopto is looking for a Senior Project Manager to own the execution behind our product initiatives — from the moment we commit to something through the day customers can use it.

Position Summary 

In this role, you will have the opportunity to do the most impactful work of your career, elevating your craft while contributing to a team that values lifelong learning.

As the Senior Project Manager, you'll report to the Program Manager and sit inside the Product team on the R&D side, which means the job runs in both directions. Upstream, you're working with Product Managers, Engineering, and Design to keep committed work moving, dependencies visible, and slippage caught early. Downstream, you're making sure Marketing has positioning, Support knows what's changing, Sales can sell it, and customers hear about it the day it goes live.

 

Most project management roles are one or the other. This one is deliberately both, because the handoffs between them are where things fall apart.

You'll take initiatives that start as a paragraph and a target quarter, break them into a plan people can act on, and keep a distributed group of teams moving in the same direction until it's out the door. This role is for someone energized rather than frustrated by ambiguity — you'll frequently be the person who turns "we're doing this next quarter" into a sequenced plan with owners and dates, and then holds everyone to it. 

You’ll also have opportunities to contribute to other initiatives that directly advance our core values and support you in elevating your craft.

How You’ll Contribute 

In this role, you will have the opportunity to

  • Own the end-to-end plan for assigned initiatives — scope, sequence, dependencies, milestones, and readiness criteria from commitment through release.

  • Break large, ambiguous initiatives into discrete workstreams with clear owners, and keep the group aligned as things shift.

  • Work alongside Product Managers and Engineering Leads to track delivery against commitments, surface slippage early, and keep cross-team dependencies visible and resolved.

  • Facilitate the sessions that move work forward — dependency reviews, cross-team planning, release readiness — and make sure they end in decisions.

  • Translate engineering blockers and technical trade-offs into clear, honest updates for Product leadership and commercial stakeholders.

  • Drive go-to-market readiness with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, Support, and Customer Success so enablement lands with the release, not after it.

  • Coordinate internal and customer-facing release communications, including release notes.

  • Build the templates, checklists, and repeatable processes that make the next release easier than the last one — using AI tooling to cut the manual overhead.

 

What Success Looks Like 

  • Within 3 months: You've built working relationships across Product, Engineering, Marketing, and Support, and you own end-to-end coordination for two or more active initiatives — running the delivery cadence with the dev teams and producing status reporting people actually read.

  • Within 6 months: You're anticipating blockers rather than reporting them, and releases you coordinate go out with GTM readiness in place on day one.

  • Within 1 year: You run our most complex, multi-team initiatives with minimal oversight, and the delivery and launch process you've built is what the rest of the team uses by default.

  • Your legacy: Panopto ships predictably, and every team knows what's coming and what they need to do about it — because you built the system that makes that true.

Values in Action

  • Customer First, Always: You proactively surface friction points in the customer experience before they are escalated — and propose solutions, not just reports.

  • Thrive Together: You share work-in-progress for early feedback, knowing that challenge improves the outcome. You separate critiques of ideas from critiques of people.

  • Elevate the Craft: You hold the bar high on your own work and invest in developing those around you. You treat every project as an opportunity to learn something new.

  • Act with Ownership: You define success by outcomes, not activity. You flag problems early and bring a proposed path forward, not just the problem.

  • Clarity Over Complexity: You default to the simpler solution. Your written communication — internal or external — is direct, specific, and free of filler.

How We Thrive

You'll join a team where we challenge ideas, not people. The Product organization exists to ideate, define, and deliver best-in-class products to our customers — assessing market trends, running competitive and customer research, and ruthlessly prioritizing the opportunities with the highest return. We hold ourselves accountable to outcomes, not activity.

 

The Foundation for Success

  • 6+ years of project or program management experience, with at least 4+ years specifically embedded within a B2B SaaS Product or R&D organization.

  • Bachelor's degree or equivalent work experience.

  • Demonstrated experience running delivery with software engineering teams and coordinating the go-to-market side of a product launch. This role does both.

  • Proven experience driving delivery for complex SaaS architectures (e.g., API integrations, multi-tenant cloud platforms, feature flags, continuous deployment release models). 

  • Working understanding of the SaaS product lifecycle and agile delivery practices, with the judgment to adapt the process to the situation rather than apply it by the book.

  • Enough technical fluency to hold a credible conversation with engineers about dependencies, trade-offs, and blockers — you don't need to write code, but you can't be a passenger in the discussion.

  • Proficiency with Jira and Confluence for planning, tracking, and documentation.

  • Strong written and verbal communication, including the ability to push back constructively on scope creep.

  • Experience working with distributed teams across multiple time zones.

  • Demonstrated track record of designing, implementing, or improving cross-functional delivery and GTM release frameworks, rather than just executing within existing ones. 

 

What Sets You Apart

  • Experience coordinating GTM launch activities with Product Marketing, Sales Enablement, or Customer Success.

  • Experience presenting, reporting delivery health, and managing trade-offs directly with VP and C-level stakeholders.

  • Experience sitting inside a Product or R&D organization rather than a central PMO.

  • Active PMP, PMI-ACP, or CSM certification.

  • Hands-on experience leveraging modern PM stacks (Jira, Confluence) and AI productivity tools to streamline status reporting, documentation, and risk analysis. 

  • Prior experience in a Product Operations (ProdOps) function.

  • Familiarity with API-based products, feature flagging, or cloud service constraints.

  • Experience in EdTech or with higher education or enterprise customers.

  • Practical use of AI tooling to accelerate planning, synthesis, and reporting work.

 

Join Us

Join Panopto and play a key role in shaping the security foundation of a platform used by millions. If you love threat modeling, automating defenses, guiding engineering teams, and turning compliance standards into practical, scalable security practices, you’ll feel right at home here.

 

Total Rewards

 

Base pay offered may vary depending on various factors, including, but not limited to: job-related knowledge, skills, experience, and other eligibility factors such as geographic location. The Total Rewards package includes competitive base pay and an opportunity to enroll in a variety of benefit programs such as health insurance, flexible spending accounts, retirement savings plans, life and disability insurance programs, and programs that provide for both paid and unpaid time away from work. At Panopto, we know that great people make an organization great. We value our people and offer employees benefits that are market competitive for our industry. For candidates hired outside the United States, compensation will be determined using local market benchmarks and will be paid in the applicable local currency. Total compensation and benefits may vary by country.

Even if you don't feel that you meet every single requirement, we still encourage you to apply. We're eager to meet people that believe in our mission and can contribute to our team in a variety of ways - not just candidates who check all the boxes. Application Review -> Recruiter Call -> Video Interview & Assessment -> Hiring Manager Call -> Interview Loop -> Debrief -> Offer

 

Our people and culture

Panopto’s mission is to be the leader in visual and audio-based learning in a capture and post-capture world. Our user base is as diverse as the world’s universities and businesses. Panopto’s commitment to fostering a fair, equitable, and inclusive culture empowers each member of our team to express their authentic selves, contribute their distinct perspectives and make a meaningful impact both individually and collectively. This inclusive environment not only encourages creativity and the free exchange of ideas but also harnesses the power of varied viewpoints. As a result, we are better equipped to tackle our most intricate challenges, leveraging the wealth of different experiences and backgrounds within our team. This collaborative spirit empowers us to challenge ideas (not people) recognizing that our shared success relies on collective wisdom. It drives us to continuously improve and innovate, ultimately elevating the quality of our products and services. It’s what sets Panopto apart as a unique and rewarding place to work.

 

Our purpose

We believe that video can have a transformative effect on learning. So we built a video knowledge management platform that helps businesses and universities improve the way that they train, teach, and share knowledge. Since 2007, we have been a pioneer in video capture software, video management, and inside-video-search technology. Panopto has been adopted by more than 1,600 companies and universities worldwide with over 11 million end users. Today, Panopto’s knowledge management platform is the largest repository of expert learning videos in the world. A proud remote-first company, Panopto is headquartered in Pittsburgh, with offices in London, Hong Kong, Singapore, and Sydney, and has received industry recognition for its innovation, rapid growth, and company culture.

title: Architect/Staff Embedded Software Engineer
description:
About OLIX

AI is growing faster than any technology in history and the explosion in demand has created a massive infrastructure gap; we can no longer build chips or power stations fast enough to keep up. The industry is still leaning on a ten-year-old hardware blueprint that has reached its limit. A new paradigm that is faster and more efficient will be the biggest economic opportunity of the next century and create the most important company of the next decade. The OLIX Decode Accelerator 1 (DX-1) is the first accelerator architected specifically for decode. Rack-scale co-design of logic, data movement, packaging, optics and interconnect enables a step change in system level performance.

The Role

As a Staff Embedded Software Engineer, you will be the design authority for a major area of the DX-1 platform firmware, within the overall platform architecture. This is the software that makes a rack of custom silicon bootable, manageable and observable, from pre-silicon simulation and FPGA prototypes through first silicon into production.

The kind of work you would own: bare-metal and real-time firmware on resource-constrained cores, embedded Linux on the platform processors, the BMC and management plane, and register-level control of the ASIC over its management link. You will report to the Platform Architect who leads the Embedded team and work closely with the FPGA, ASIC and Systems Software teams.

You bring exceptional depth on both sides of the hardware-software boundary, the judgment to identify what matters most and why, and the ability to influence and align engineering teams without relying on formal authority. It is a hands-on individual-contributor role. We will judge it by what others can build on: specs other teams work to, firmware that is ready when the hardware is, and designs that still hold up a year on.

Responsibilities

  • Lead a major area of the platform firmware. Boot and update, platform management or register-level control of the ASIC, agreed with you based on your strengths. Own its design, interfaces and roadmap within the platform architecture, and be accountable for it reaching production.

  • Make the interfaces explicit. Write down the contracts your area depends on and exposes, from register maps to update and telemetry flows, so the teams on either side can build against them.

  • Support bring-up and validation. When a bring-up or test problem turns out to be in boot, drivers or the management plane, you are the person who gets called. Help the teams running it get to the cause, and write up what you find so nobody has to rediscover it.

  • Define failure and update behaviour. How a fault in a node, rail or link is contained so it does not take out the rack, what gets logged so we can find the cause, and what happens if a firmware update is interrupted halfway.

  • Build things the team keeps using. Reference implementations, firmware tests on the infrastructure the validation teams already run, and contributions to the device models.

  • Pick the problems that matter. Identify the highest-impact technical risks in the platform firmware and at its interfaces to the FPGA and silicon teams, and make sure they get solved.

  • Develop the senior engineers around you. Review their designs as well as their code, set them up to lead areas of their own, and take an active part in hiring.

Skills & Experience

  • Depth on both sides of the hardware-software boundary. Bare-metal or RTOS firmware on resource-constrained cores, and embedded Linux BSP work (Yocto/OpenEmbedded, U-Boot or UEFI, drivers, device tree).

  • Systems fundamentals. Memory ordering and barriers, coherent and non-coherent shared memory, synchronisation with and without atomics, interrupt latency, and timing and memory-bandwidth budgets.

  • Taken firmware through a silicon or board bring-up, from pre-silicon simulation or emulation and FPGA prototypes to first power-on, and able to walk us through what went wrong and how it was found. More than one generation, or firmware for an ASIC whose tape-out you worked towards, is a significant advantage.

  • Platform management in a rack-scale context. OpenBMC or equivalent, Redfish, PLDM over MCTP, and the buses underneath (I2C/SMBus/PMBus, SPI, UART), including power sequencing and fault isolation.

  • Register-level control of an ASIC or large FPGA over a management link, including against a simulation model before silicon exists. Precision timing (IEEE 1588 PTP, White Rabbit, SyncE), SerDes or optical link bring-up, or secure boot would all be an advantage.

  • Technical leadership without formal authority. A specification, methodology, or tool you authored that teams outside your own adopted and still use, and the design document behind it.

  • Outstanding technical communicator. You can articulate architectural decisions and their consequences clearly to engineers, managers and senior leadership alike, and write design documents that other teams build to.

Compensation & Equity

  • Competitive Salary: Commensurate with your experience, skills, and location

  • Equity & Ownership: Meaningful stock options. You’re not just joining the mission; you’re owning a piece of it

  • Proximity Bonus: We value your time. To minimise your commute and maximise your life, we offer an annual Living-Local Bonus if your residence is within 20 minutes of the office

  • Retirement Benefits: Employer-contributed retirement plans to help you build long-term financial security.

We are generally unable to consider applicants whose most recent citizenship or permanent residence is in certain restricted countries (currently including Iran, North Korea, Syria, Cuba, Russia, Belarus, China, Hong Kong, Macau, and Venezuela). Applicants who have subsequently obtained citizenship or permanent residency in another country not subject to these restrictions may still be eligible.

title: Finance Manager / Accountant
description:
Future Kitchens is the operating system for virtual food brands. We build delivery-first consumer brands like SmashClub® and KNOCKOUT®, and plug them into partner restaurants across Switzerland. 55+ partner locations. And we're just getting started.

We're operators, not a consultancy. We move fast, we keep it concrete, and we build systems that scale.

Tasks

You own the numbers. All of them.

This is not a back-office bookkeeping job. You'll run the finance function of a fast-growing food company, and you'll build the automated accounting infrastructure that lets our restaurant partners run their virtual restaurant business without ever touching a spreadsheet. What you build becomes a core part of our partner product.

You report directly to the CEO and work closely with the Growth and Operations teams.

What you'll do

Run the books. Full ownership of accounting for Future Kitchens AG: accounts payable and receivable, reconciliations, month-end close, VAT filings, all under Swiss OR requirements.

Prepare weekly partner payouts. Every week, 55+ partner restaurants get paid. You reconcile platform revenue (Just Eat, Uber Eats, Wolt), apply the commercial terms, and make sure every payout is correct and on time. Partners trust us with their revenue. You're the reason that trust holds.

Prepare financial statements. Monthly, quarterly, and annual statements for management, the board, and investors. Clean, on time, decision-ready.

Build financial dashboards. Real-time visibility on revenue, margins, payouts, and store-level performance. For management, for the board, and for partners. If it matters, it's on a dashboard, and it's current.

Build the automated accounting practice for partners. This is the big one. You'll design and roll out a fully automated accounting service for our restaurant partners: payout reconciliation, revenue reporting, and clean books, delivered as a product, not a service desk. Manual work is a bug, not a feature.

Run payroll. Monthly payroll for all internal staff: salaries, AHV/IV/EO, ALV, BVG, accident insurance, withholding tax, and annual salary certificates. Accurate, compliant, zero drama.

Requirements

What you bring

  • Completed commercial or finance education (Fachausweis Finanz- und Rechnungswesen, ideally on the path to expert level, or equivalent)
  • 3+ years of hands-on accounting experience in Switzerland, ideally in a high-transaction-volume environment (gastronomy, retail, e-commerce, marketplaces)
  • Solid command of Swiss accounting standards (OR), Swiss VAT, and Swiss payroll including social insurance
  • Strong systems mindset: you automate before you delegate, and you'd rather build a workflow once than repeat a task weekly
  • Confident with modern accounting software (Bexio, Abacus, or similar) and comfortable connecting tools via integrations and automation platforms
  • Advanced Excel / Google Sheets skills; experience with BI or dashboard tools is a strong plusFluent German, professional English
  • You're precise under deadline pressure. Weekly payouts don't wait.

Nice to have

  • Experience with delivery platform reporting and reconciliation (Just Eat, Uber Eats, Wolt)
  • Experience building finance processes from scratch in a startup or scale-up
  • Exposure to AI-assisted workflows and no-code automation (Make, Zapier, or similar)

Benefits

  • Full ownership of the finance function at one of Switzerland's fastest-growing food tech companies
  • A greenfield mandate: build the automated accounting product for 55+ (soon 100) partner restaurants
  • Direct line to the CEO, real influence on how the company runs
  • A team that ships, not a committee that meets
  • Office in Zürich

  • Team-oriented mindset with a strong focus on driving customer value and achieving measurable outcomes.

  • Be part of a fast-growing AI company, working on cutting-edge conversational AI products used by leading enterprises.

About the role

Luminovo builds software that powers the electronics supply chain — and we're growing our OEM segment across the DACH market. As a BDR based in Germany, you'll own the top of the funnel: turning cold outreach into qualified pipeline for our Account Executives.

This is a high-impact role for someone who believes cold calling isn't dead, thrives on outbound, and wants to grow into a closing role in B2B SaaS.

What you'll do

  • Run multichannel outbound sequences — email, phone, LinkedIn, and events — targeting technical buyers at OEMs across the DACH region

  • Use tools like Apollo, Clay, Lusha, and LinkedIn Sales Navigator to build and work targeted lead lists

  • Qualify prospects through cold call sequences to identify ICP fit

  • Hand off warm opportunities to Account Executives with clean notes and context

  • Track your own metrics and bring frontline market insights back to sales and marketing leadership

Who you are

  • Required BDR/SDR experience in B2B SaaS (or strong hunger to break in)

  • Fluent in German and English — you'll be reaching buyers across the DACH region

  • Comfortable with rejection and energized by outbound

  • Driven to grow into an Account Executive role and willing to earn it

  • Bonus: experience or genuine curiosity in electronics, manufacturing, or hardware

  • Nice to have: you use AI as more than a better search engine. Ideally you've built your own automations, workflows, or tools — we care about what you've actually shipped, not what you've read them

Work setup

Remote from Germany. Munich is our global HQ; we also have a Berlin hub.

Travel

We meet regularly for team retreats and selected industry events, so expect occasional travel. We cover the costs.

Why Luminovo

  • Join a well-funded SaaS scaleup at a pivotal growth stage

  • Clear path to Account Executive with a team invested in your development

  • Hybrid in Munich or Berlin with an international, high-performance team

🤓 Whom you’ll be working with

  • Dasha, our BDR Lead

  • Clifton, our VP Global Sales

  • Inga, our pioneer AE in the OEM market segment

  • Seba, one of our founders, supporting the OEM GTM team

  • Max, our Revenue Operations Team Lead, and his team

  • Our Product Managers, so you fully understand our product roadmap, potential constraints, and share product-related customer feedback

⚡️ Skills, knowledge, and expertise

Just so you know – we purposefully did not create a standard list of minimum qualifications for this role. We care much more about your motivation and ability to help us accelerate technical progress than we care just about your CV. If you're interested to find out more about why we banned requirements from our performance profiles – see here.

⚡️ About Luminovo

Luminovo is the first electronics supply chain platform that unites all data, processes, and stakeholders in the trillion-dollar electronics industry.

We fundamentally believe that technology is the best tool that humankind has developed to tackle the biggest challenges we face as a society today. And we want to do our share in accelerating technological progress.

We bring innovations to life faster and cheaper by creating a more connected and resilient electronics supply chain.

title: Senior iOS Developer (Remote)
description:
About Finom
 
Finom is a European tech startup headquartered in Amsterdam, and we’re on a journey towards revolutionizing the financial landscape for entrepreneurs worldwide. Our mission is to develop an all-in-one financial B2B solution that integrates banking functions, accounting, financial management, and invoicing into a seamless, mobile-first platform.
 
We recently closed a €115 million Series C equity round (around $133 million), bringing our total funding to approximately $346 million. This significant investment follows a $105 million growth funding round from General Catalyst, a long-term backer since 2021 known for supporting companies like Airbnb, HubSpot, KAYAK, and Stripe.
 
Finom's platform goes beyond traditional banking, offering invoicing and a growing suite of features, including AI-enabled accounting, aiming to simplify financial management for entrepreneurs. We're actively expanding our reach across key EU markets like Germany, France, the Netherlands, Italy, and Spain.
 
At Finom, we’re not just redefining the entrepreneurial experience — we’re empowering our employees to make a real difference. Your work matters, and your impact extends far beyond product metrics. We nurture innovation and an inspiring work environment where bold ideas thrive, prioritizing thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and our business as a whole.
 
Maintaining our start-up spirit, we prioritize thorough research, swift implementation of solutions, and ensuring that every effort we make benefits our users, employees, partners, and, of course, our business.

The Role

For hundreds of thousands of European entrepreneurs, our iOS app is Finom. It's how they check their cash flow over morning coffee, approve a payment between client meetings, and freeze a card the moment something looks off. We're mobile-first by conviction, not convenience — the app isn't a companion to the "real" product; it is the product. And as an AI-native platform, the features you build increasingly carry intelligence inside them: AI-powered accounting, smart categorization, and agentic workflows that quietly save business owners hours every week. When you ship something great, someone somewhere feels it the same day.

That's why we're not looking for someone to implement tickets. We're looking for a Senior Mobile (iOS) Engineer who thinks like a product builder — someone who cares deeply about the "why" behind what they're building, challenges assumptions when needed, and proactively spots opportunities to create better outcomes.

You'll be embedded in a cross-functional domain team — Backend, Mobile, ML/AI, QA, Design, and Product — that owns a shared product area end-to-end. No handoff culture, no "not my layer": everyone in the team is solving the same customer problem, and you'll shape solutions from the first product conversation to the moment the feature is live in users' hands. Fewer silos means more flow — and real, end-to-end ownership.


What You Will Be Doing

How We Build

Agentic development is table stakes at Finom — for every craft, mobile included. Our engineers work with Claude Code and similar harnesses daily, and we've made it a first-class part of how the company operates, not an individual productivity hack. We follow a shared SDLC approach built around Spec-Driven Development (SDD): features start as clear, reviewable specs that both humans and AI agents execute against, powered by a shared AI development toolbelt and a growing library of skills, rules, and context maintained across guilds. You won't be figuring out AI-assisted development alone — you'll join an engineering organization that has already invested in the infrastructure, standards, and shared practices, and you'll be expected to use them, improve them, and raise the bar for others.

What You'll Do

  • Design and build new features for our iOS application, used daily by business owners across Europe: multi-account cash flow management, banking transactions and payments, physical and virtual card issuance and control, and AI-powered accounting automation.

  • Own outcomes, not just code. You'll follow your features into analytics, jump into customer issues without being prompted, and care about whether what you shipped actually moved the needle.

  • Build polished, responsive UIs with UIKit and SwiftUI — in a financial app, trust is built (or lost) in the details.

  • Drive technical decisions within your domain, discuss trade-offs openly with product managers, and explain constraints clearly to non-technical stakeholders.

  • Raise the bar on engineering quality — automated testing, thorough code reviews, and mobile security best practices are non-negotiable in a regulated fintech.

  • Mentor the engineers around you and contribute to CI/CD pipelines, tooling, and mobile best practices across the team.


Who You Are

Who You Are

You're pragmatic, learn quickly, and have a proven track record of shipping products that matter. Above all, you're curious — about the product, the users, the business, and how your technical decisions impact all three.

Curiosity. You want to understand the "why" behind every feature. You ask what problem it solves, question whether there's a simpler path, and explore how your decisions ripple into product, users, and revenue.

Business acumen. You connect your work to company objectives. You understand the "so what" behind every decision, and you'd rather ship the feature that moves the right metric than the one that's merely interesting to build.

Communication. You communicate clearly and concisely in English across technical and non-technical audiences — from fellow engineers to PMs to business stakeholders — and you genuinely enjoy the dynamics of a cross-functional team.

T-shapedness. Your iOS craft runs deep, but your curiosity runs wide. You'll peek at the backend contracts, ask questions about the ML models, and dive into analytics to understand how your features perform.

Ownership. You take responsibility not just for your code, but for the outcomes. You move without being prompted — whether that's improving team processes, jumping on a production issue, or mentoring a colleague.

Your Experience Includes

  • 5+ years of commercial iOS development with strong knowledge of Swift.

  • Deep understanding of OOP, SOLID principles, and design patterns.

  • Practical experience with the VIPER architectural pattern and the Coordinator navigation pattern — and the judgment to know when a simpler approach serves the product better.

  • Excellent knowledge of UIKit and experience (or a strong desire to grow) with SwiftUI.

  • Experience with layout development in code, particularly using SnapKit or similar tools.

  • Ability to write unit and UI tests.

  • Confidence with Git / GitLab, including setting up and maintaining GitLab CI/CD.

  • Hands-on experience with agentic development tools (Claude Code, Cursor, Copilot, or similar) as part of your daily workflow — writing prompts, configuring rules and skills, and critically evaluating AI-generated output with tests, linters, and review. This is table stakes for all engineering crafts at Finom, mobile included.

  • A builder's mentality: you care deeply about shipping great products, not just writing great code.

    • Experience profiling and optimizing UI performance — reducing rendering bottlenecks and hitting smooth 60/120fps on iOS.

    • Hands-on work with performance tooling: Instruments, XCTest, or similar.

Unlock your inner entrepreneur and align your aspirations with ours through our Stock Options Program. This exciting opportunity is available to every team member, from junior team members to our founders.

Finom stands by you at every step, embodying our commitment to your well-being and success reflected in our modern, friendly, and eco-conscious corporate culture. We offer constant support and care to ensure your Finom experience is successful and fulfilling.

Immerse yourself in our exclusive Work & Swim Program. Spend one month in a comfortable corporate apartment in enchanting Cyprus. It's the ideal opportunity to strike the perfect work-life balance while enjoying breathtaking Mediterranean views.
